title: Start here
summary: Visual C · Stage 1 A field guide to C execution evidence. Stage 1 accepts C source and a build configuration, compiles and observes a bounded primary execution, exports a schema-v2 trace, and provides immutable, validated, trace-s
text: Visual C · Stage 1 A field guide to C execution evidence. Stage 1 accepts C source and a build configuration, compiles and observes a bounded primary execution, exports a schema-v2 trace, and provides immutable, validated, trace-scoped evidence to future consumers. This site documents the implemented Trace Engine and Trace Parser. Stage 2's C Semantic Engine is not implemented here. {{diagram:architecture}} Choose a route - New to the system? Start with the architecture(architecture.html), then the debugger lifecycle(engine-debugger.html), data model(model.html), and the API walkthrough(usage.html). - Adding an engine feature? Read compilation(engine-build.html), variable capture(engine-memory.html), heap telemetry(engine-heap.html), and budgets(engine-limits.html) before editing Stage 1. - Consuming evidence? Read parser ingestion(parser-ingestion.html), validation(parser-validation.html), semantic confidence(parser-semantic.html), bounded pages(parser-consumer.html), and the Stage 2 handoff(handoff.html). - Looking up a type? Use the public API(api.html), schema/identity tables(schema.html), right-hand page contents, or offline search (/). Level 1 · The central idea A debugger can say “at this stop, these bytes were readable.” It cannot, by that observation alone, say “this pointer definitely came from allocation 7,” “these bytes were initialized,” or “every child process was observed.” Visual C records both the useful observation and its uncertainty. A consumer should keep addresses separate from identities(schema.htmlidentity-domains), and distinguish a structurally sound trace from a complete execution(parser-validation.htmllevel-2-architecture). Level 2 · What ships The Trace Engine(engine-build.html) uses GCC, GDB/MI2, DWARF and optional Clang syntax; a linked C allocator wrapper records its own events. Valgrind and sanitizers are separate executions. One DebugSessionTrace(model.html) contains checkpoints, instruction attempts, gaps, heap lifetimes, stage outcomes and reports. The Trace Parser(parser-ingestion.html) loads the JSON once, builds position-only indexes, and exposes borrowed, validated, explicitly paginated queries. This boundary is deliberate: Stage 1 captures evidence; Stage 2 may later interpret C-language meaning without changing recorded history. Level 3 · Begin in code - Recording entry point: src/trace.rs::trace_program(TraceConfig); schema: src/models.rs::DebugSessionTrace. - Parser entry point: src/trace_parser/mod.rs::TraceStore::open; validation: TraceStore::validated_semantic() in semantic.rs. - Stable consumer example: examples/stage1_public_consumer_audit.rs; runnable introduction in Practical usage(usage.html). NOTE: The Stage 1 freeze is approved within a bounded evidence scope, not as a sandbox, a whole-process-tree tracer, a memory-initialization oracle, or a guarantee of assembled-trace RAM. Read the precise limits(handoff.htmlknown-limitations). How to use this site offline Open index.html directly in a browser. No network is required. Search, diagrams, themes, code styles, navigation and content are local. The README(README.md) explains regeneration; every generated page is checked in alongside its Markdown source.

title: System architecture
summary: Architecture · one recording, many qualified readers Level 1 · Intuition The system has two non-interchangeable jobs. The Trace Engine gathers bounded observations while a compiled C program runs under GDB; the Trace Parser lets o
text: Architecture · one recording, many qualified readers Level 1 · Intuition The system has two non-interchangeable jobs. The Trace Engine gathers bounded observations while a compiled C program runs under GDB; the Trace Parser lets other code navigate that finished recording safely. A JSON trace is the contract between them. No parser query can revisit an inferior or recover an event that the engine did not capture. {{diagram:architecture}} Level 2 · Pipeline and boundaries 1. A TraceConfig describes sources, program arguments, tools, limits and optional tracing modes. GCC builds a debug executable with an allocator wrapper and prepares a separately sanitized executable. Compilation failure has diagnostics but no fabricated stops. 2. The engine extracts static DWARF(engine-metadata.html) from the GCC artifact and optionally runs a Clang AST pass. GDB/MI observes one followed inferior, source checkpoints and instruction attempts. The wrapper appends PID-local heap events(engine-heap.html). Analyses have separately recorded outcomes. 3. One DebugSessionTrace preserves original observations, metadata, reports and scope/gaps(engine-limits.html). The recorder can append JSONL records during execution, but a JSONL journal is not a complete JSON trace. 4. TraceStore::open parses the JSON, checks schema version and builds immutable position indexes(parser-indexes.html). validated_semantic() performs one opt-in deep validation pass; TP-7 composes qualified borrowed views in explicit pages of at most 128. 5. A future Stage 2 consumer may compute explanations from these citations. Its interpretations must not be confused with primary observations. {{diagram:compilation}} Distinct evidence providers Provider What it knows What it does not establish --------- GCC + DWARF Compiled types, declarations, debug layout, diagnostics Dynamic value or initializer execution GDB/MI Stopped frame, source line, values and bounded memory reads All execution between stops or other processes C allocation wrapper PID/sequence-tagged intercepted allocator calls Internal allocations in unwrapped libraries Clang AST (optional) Candidate syntax and source spans That an expression executed Valgrind / ASan / UBSan Diagnostics from independent reproductions Identity of a primary-run allocation Level 3 · Trace through the implementation src/trace.rs::trace_program calls ExecutionLimits::validate, enters a supervisor::scope, probes tools, invokes compiler::compile_project, extracts DWARF with dwarf::extract_excluding, and conditionally runs clang_ast::analyze. Its stopped loop cooperates with src/gdb_mi.rs, src/recorder.rs and src/allocation_tracker.rs. After reconstructing lifetimes and optional evidence fusion(engine-metadata.html), src/models.rs defines the serializable result. src/json_export.rs writes an individually capped JSON document. src/trace_parser/mod.rs::TraceStore::assemble stores Arc<DebugSessionTrace plus Arc<TraceIndexes without copying source records. rust // Core architecture signatures; source: src/trace.rs and src/trace_parser. pub async fn trace_program(config: TraceConfig) - Result<DebugSessionTrace; // TraceStore's public entry point (method declaration): pub fn open(path: impl AsRef<Path, options: TraceLoadOptions) - Result<Self; // Constructing this view runs one opt-in validation pass: pub fn validated_semantic(&self) - ValidatedSemanticView<'_; WARNING: The above is a signature excerpt, not a single compilable Rust module; Result and Self come from their respective modules. The runnable importable version is on Practical usage(usage.html). A question to ask at every boundary Is this datum an observation, a static candidate, a recorded association, a validation finding or a future interpretation? See confidence(parser-semantic.html) for the rules that keep those categories separate.

title: Compilation & diagnostics
summary: Compilation and compiler diagnostics Level 1 · Intuition Visual C needs a real executable with debug information, not a speculative reading of C text. It runs GCC on the user's sources, preserving warnings/errors as structured dia
text: Compilation and compiler diagnostics Level 1 · Intuition Visual C needs a real executable with debug information, not a speculative reading of C text. It runs GCC on the user's sources, preserving warnings/errors as structured diagnostics. If compilation fails, the trace records that failure; it does not pretend the debugger ran. The same project can produce a separate sanitizer build for a later diagnostic execution. {{diagram:compilation}} Level 2 · Build lifecycle BuildConfig names the primary C file, additional sources, object files, defines, include/library paths, flags and working directory. TraceConfig adds inferior arguments, resource limits, output path, optional Clang pass and tool overrides. compiler::compile_project builds the debug variant with c_runtime/alloc_tracker.c via -Wl,--wrap=malloc, calloc, realloc, free, and a separate ASan/UBSan variant without the wrapper. User flags follow engine defaults; explicit user overrides can change fidelity and must be considered when interpreting a trace. The compiler probes whether GCC supports JSON diagnostics, SARIF-to-stderr or plain-text fallback; it normalizes diagnostic kind, file, line, column and message. Tool processes are supervised with bounded output and deadline. When GCC fails, compiled_successfully=false, execution_status=compile_failed, compiler stage failed, debugger and later analyses skipped, and snapshots=. A compilation pipeline failure (tool launch/deadline) is recorded separately from GCC rejecting source. A successful debug build enables DWARF extraction and GDB control. Sanitizer compilation is not evidence that the sanitized process later reproduced a crash. Level 3 · Files, signatures and example - src/config.rs::{BuildConfig, TraceConfig, SanitizerTrigger} describe the request. - src/compiler.rs::{CompileOptions, compile_project, detect_diagnostics_format} handle both build variants and error formats. src/trace.rs::trace_program_inner assigns stage_results.compiler and short-circuits on failed compilation. - src/models.rs::{CompilerDiagnostic, StageResults, StageResult} preserve structured outcomes. src/supervisor.rs owns subprocess groups and session deadlines. c // Source fixture: fixtures/c/phase8b_defined.c (abridged) int oracle_global = 41; static int checkpoint(struct Packet packet, int alias, int heap, int sum) { volatile int value = packet-items1 + alias + heap2 + sum + oracle_global; return value; } sh cargo build --release target/release/c-trace-engine fixtures/c/phase8b_defined.c \ --trace-mode dual --max-steps 350 --timeout 50 --no-pretty \ --sanitizer-trigger never --output /tmp/visual-c-defined.json From the final integrated audit(../stage1-final-audit.md), a deliberately invalid return missing_symbol; produced an engine JSON trace with execution_status="compile_failed", one compiler diagnostic and zero snapshots/events. Consult practical usage(usage.htmllevel-2-run-a-recording) for safe output inspection and diagnostics(engine-diagnostics.html) for independent analysis stages. NOTE: Tool availability is checked before compilation: GCC and GDB are required. Missing Valgrind or addr2line is reported and qualified, not a successful zero-error analysis. No part of this pipeline is a sandbox for hostile C.

title: GDB/MI and checkpoints
summary: GDB/MI execution and checkpoints Level 1 · Intuition A stopped program is observable; running code between stops is not automatically known. The GDB/MI2 driver sends commands, waits for the corresponding responses and asynchronous
text: GDB/MI execution and checkpoints Level 1 · Intuition A stopped program is observable; running code between stops is not automatically known. The GDB/MI2 driver sends commands, waits for the corresponding responses and asynchronous stops, and inspects bounded source state. At a stop the PC names the next instruction. The engine records an instruction attempt from that before address and a next address only when observed. Source checkpoints are selected stops, not a reconstruction of every intermediate state. {{diagram:checkpoint}} Level 2 · Command/response lifecycle A GDB session launches the debug binary, stops at entry and identifies a followed inferior. The engine classifies frames as user, runtime, library or unknown; collects stack/source context at checkpoints; drains allocator telemetry while the inferior is stopped; snapshots variables, bytes and live heap subject to budgets; and records that snapshot with a monotonic stop_id. In dual mode it attempts -exec-step-instruction and separately waits for stopped (a tokened ^running is only an acknowledgement). The InstructionEvent stores the before PC, attempted event_id, source context, thread/PID, stop_id_before/optional stop_id_after, outcome and optional next PC. An async missing-stop wait is classified differently from a whole-session deadline; a missing response poisons the command session rather than giving late output to a future command. Outcomes include completed, faulted, interrupted and unknown. Breakpoints do not prove the attempted instruction completed. Library/source stepping introduces TraceGap(model.htmlevents-gaps-and-checkpoints) records with attempted-position boundaries, not guessed counts. A user callback can be captured by bounded entry-breakpoint discovery; unobserved callbacks cannot be inferred from a static source call. GDB is in all-stop mode, but external processes are not paused and a multi-threaded selected-thread timeline is incomplete. A forked child is not promised GDB snapshots. Worked stop → parser query At source line 15 of fixtures/c/phase8b_defined.c, the audited live capture recorded an integer sum with displayed value "10" and raw bytes "0a000000" (Linux little-endian), while native GDB in a separate run independently printed sum=10. A later TraceStore can retrieve the snapshot using its vector index, and checkpoint_summary() can page its variables. Neither the stop ID nor the value of instruction_position should be used as that vector index. See the API walkthrough(usage.htmlcheckpoints-and-paging). Level 3 · Source and invariants - src/gdb_mi.rs owns MI command tokens, async records, stop backlog, frame parsing, selected-thread tracking and memory reads. src/mi_parser.rs parses MI syntax. - src/trace.rs orchestrates the stop loop and push_snapshot. src/recorder.rs::{checkpoint, event, gap, event_outcome} appends bounded canonical records and journal lines. - src/models.rs::{SnapshotObservation, InstructionEvent, TraceGap} defines the serializable identities. src/trace_parser/indexes.rs::OrderingFacts enables binary search only when order is verified. json {"step_index":0,"observation":{"stop_id":1,"instruction_position":0,"heap_event_count":0}} The JSON above is illustrative and deliberately partial; a real ExecutionSnapshot has required file, function, call stack and variable fields. stop_id=1 is a debugger stop counter, step_index=0 a snapshot vector index, and instruction_position=0 a count of attempts before this stop. See schema identity domains(schema.htmlidentity-domains). WARNING: Recording a checkpoint_id on an instruction event associates it with the most recent checkpoint, not a claim that its instruction happened precisely at the checkpoint stop or that a source-line AST expression executed.

title: Frames, variables & memory
summary: Stack frames, variables and raw memory Level 1 · Intuition A displayed debugger value is an observation made at one stopped moment, not a proof of C-language initialization. Visual C records where a variable lived, what GDB could
text: Stack frames, variables and raw memory Level 1 · Intuition A displayed debugger value is an observation made at one stopped moment, not a proof of C-language initialization. Visual C records where a variable lived, what GDB could display, whether bytes were actually read, and which limits prevented a fuller read. Function calls introduce new frame activations; two locals named n in different recursive calls are not the same variable. {{diagram:stack}} Level 2 · At a stopped checkpoint A ExecutionSnapshot has variables for frame 0 and a bounded optional caller_frames vector of FrameVariables. Globals/file statics live in snapshot.observation.globals. The stack itself is call_stack: Vec<StackFrameInfo: frame level=0 is innermost, while caller_frames vector position is not a GDB level. Per-thread activation IDs and lexical scope IDs distinguish shadowing across calls. With GDB's embedded Python support, lexical block bounds and Symbol.value(frame) aid identity and correct shadowed-variable reads; unavailable probes use explicitly qualified fallback identity. Scope activity alone never means a declaration's initializer has executed. VariableInfo.address is the address of the variable's storage. For a pointer, points_to is the stored target address. target.address_match_allocation_id is only a numeric containment candidate. Reused addresses are ambiguous; pointer provenance(parser-semantic.htmlpointer-and-memory-confidence) must not be inferred from a current address match. read_status describes GDB's displayed value, bytes_status the byte capture, memory_evidence requested/captured/extent/status, and initialization_status is a separate (often unknown) dimension. A raw_bytes_hex prefix can be valid with an explicitly unobserved tail; unobserved does not necessarily mean unreadable. Optional per-instruction --memory-region reads are exact only at their own recorded instruction stop; earlier checkpoint bytes are last-known elsewhere. Worked call c // Illustrative C; see fixtures/c/recursive.c for the real tested fixture. int recurse(int value) { if (value == 0) return 1; return value recurse(value - 1); } When recurse(3) calls recurse(2), the second frame has a distinct activation. The audited engine trace with limits.max_caller_frames=3 captured 45 caller-frame entries across 26 snapshots, not an unlimited call history. Each checkpoint is a historical observation: later returns/frees must not mutate earlier captures. The TP-7 frame activation(parser-consumer.htmllevel-3-real-signatures-and-bounded-traversal) query only resolves within one retained snapshot. Level 3 · Where to look - src/gdb_mi.rs extracts StackFrameInfo, RawVariable and bounded GDB reads; src/trace.rs::push_snapshot collects checkpoint state, heap blocks and caller frames. - src/memory.rs enriches byte/target observations; src/recorder.rs::set_validity keeps display/byte status distinct. src/dwarf.rs::associate correlates unique declarations without replacing GDB values. - src/models.rs::{ExecutionSnapshot, SnapshotObservation, VariableInfo, MemoryEvidence, FrameVariables, ScopeStatus, DataValidity} is the schema; src/trace_parser/semantic.rs::MemoryEvidenceView qualifies captured byte ranges without decoding C semantics. json {"name":"sum","value":"10","raw_bytes_hex":"0a000000","read_status":"valid","bytes_status":"valid"} This is an abridged excerpt of the audited phase8b_defined.c:15 variable, not a stand-alone VariableInfo document. Four readable bytes show a captured representation of 10, not a proof of prior initialization. Consult data model(model.htmlvariables-bytes-and-heap) and confidence(parser-semantic.html). NOTE: Caller capture defaults to max_caller_frames=0. A missing caller vector is not evidence that the program had no caller. Per-snapshot and per-variable read budgets may truncate capture without invalidating all other observations.

title: DWARF, Clang & fusion
summary: DWARF, Clang AST and evidence fusion Level 1 · Intuition Static metadata helps explain what a stopped value might be: DWARF identifies the compiler's types and declarations; optional Clang AST identifies syntax and source spans. G
text: DWARF, Clang AST and evidence fusion Level 1 · Intuition Static metadata helps explain what a stopped value might be: DWARF identifies the compiler's types and declarations; optional Clang AST identifies syntax and source spans. GDB supplies dynamic runtime values. None of these static sources alone proves that a C expression executed. Fusion supplies carefully qualified links between existing records, never replacement values or invented writes. {{diagram:metadata}} Level 2 · The three evidence streams dwarf::extract_excluding scans the actual GCC-built debug artifact, excluding the injected tracker source, and builds a bounded TypeRegistry of units, type entries and declarations. dwarf::associate attaches uniquely correlated type/declaration IDs to runtime variables, preserving GDB-observed addresses and sizes. Clang is opt-in (--clang-ast): clang_ast::analyze parses source syntax into a SourceMetadataRegistry; a missing tool/partial translation unit is recorded, not silently treated as an empty program. Clang's view of preprocessing/type layout may differ from GCC's; cross-provider correlation may be unavailable. After runtime capture and heap reconstruction, evidence::fuse runs once. src/evidence/declarations.rs links eligible static declarations/members, source_links.rs considers runtime/declaration references, heap.rs records heap-call candidates/ambiguities, and validation.rs rejects unsafe links. EvidenceFusionSummary counts only serialized links and rejected links. No GDB command is issued during fusion, no registry is copied per snapshot, and absence of both providers leaves fusion absent. The parser's TP-2 metadata index maps string IDs to positions, not cloned declarations. Worked ambiguity Two heap-call expressions on one source line—or a macro expanding to one—can share a line with a recorded allocation event. The relationship can be a candidate or ambiguous; a same-line match is never a dynamic expression-to-event identity. TP-6 source_expression(id).execution_confidence remains Unavailable even if heap_call_candidates exist. This is important when writing future Stage 2 explanations(handoff.htmllevel-2-the-freeze-contract). Level 3 · Files and API - src/dwarf.rs::{TypeRegistry, extract_excluding, associate} reads ELF/DWARF, matches unique declarations and reports missing/ambiguous data. - src/clang_ast.rs::{SourceMetadataRegistry, analyze, correlate_heap_calls} produces optional static syntax. - src/evidence/mod.rs::fuse and src/evidence/{declarations,source_links,heap,validation}.rs perform bounded reconciliation; src/models.rs::EvidenceFusionSummary serializes counts. - TraceStore::type_entry(id), dwarf_declaration(id), source_declaration(id), source_expression(id) return borrowed indexed metadata; ValidatedSemanticView::source_expression(id) adds confidence and indexed candidate/ambiguity event positions. rust // Real TP-6 API; expression IDs belong to this trace, not to other runs. let expression = validated.source_expression(expression_id); let syntax = expression.expression; // Option<&SourceExpression let execution = expression.execution_confidence; // Unavailable on sound traces for candidate in expression.call_sites() { let _ = (candidate.event_position, candidate.event); } The snippet assumes validated and expression_id are already defined; run the complete parser walkthrough(usage.htmllevel-3-load-and-validate) first. See the public API reference(api.htmllevel-3-signatures-and-contracts) for signatures. WARNING: “source line observed” ≠ “specific AST expression executed.” Never use an AST call candidate to grant pointer provenance or to allocate a new runtime lifetime.

title: Allocation lifetimes
summary: Allocation events, lifetimes and realloc Level 1 · Intuition The same numeric address can host multiple unrelated allocations over time. Stage 1 assigns a lifetime ID to each intercepted allocation, records events that affect it,
text: Allocation events, lifetimes and realloc Level 1 · Intuition The same numeric address can host multiple unrelated allocations over time. Stage 1 assigns a lifetime ID to each intercepted allocation, records events that affect it, and keeps snapshots immutable. A current pointer address can match a block's extent without proving which lifetime produced the pointer. realloc can retire one lifetime and create a linked successor; a failed call must not retire the original. {{diagram:heap}} Level 2 · Telemetry → reconstructed lifetimes The debug binary links c_runtime/alloc_tracker.c with --wrap for malloc, calloc, realloc and free calls from linked objects. A fixed-size C table tracks address→local-ID/size; each wrapper calls the actual allocator once, writes a PID/monotonic per-PID sequence line to a dedicated file, and preserves the return value. A recursion guard prevents tracker reentry. Rust's EventTailer reads completed records; HeapTimeline::ingest reconstructs events and block state, tracks gaps/duplicates/out-of-order rows and assembles AllocationLifetime. Events are drained at stops before source state is read. Caller PCs can be resolved while the inferior is alive using /proc/PID/maps, ELF load bias and addr2line; unresolved PCs stay recorded. malloc(A) creates ID 1. free(A) closes its lifetime; later malloc(A) starts ID 2 even at the same address. A successful moving realloc retires an old ID and gives the new block a linked ID; the current C wrapper also issues a new lifetime ID for a successful in-place realloc (ok_same), even though the address does not change. A failed realloc leaves the original block alive. Under glibc, realloc(ptr,0) may free the original and return NULL; the engine can emit a terminal Reallocated event with the same old/new ID, null address and size zero. This is not a new predecessor edge. Successful successor identity is certified by event/lifetime validation(parser-validation.htmlrealloc-link-verification), not by matching addresses. Evidence Meaning Caution --------- HeapEvent Ingestion-order wrapper event, PID, sequence, IDs, kind, optional address ID 0 is untracked; internal library allocators may be invisible HeapBlockInfo Final/historical state, optional realloc predecessor Freed block bytes are historical; check observed_at_stop AllocationLifetime PID, allocation sequence, optional free sequence Complete observed-PID history is not a fork census HeapHistoryCoverage Gaps, transport, ACK, caps, process scope complete=true has a specific observed-PID scope Level 3 · C/Rust boundary and example c // Source: fixtures/c/realloc_move.c (excerpt) char p = malloc(32); char guard = malloc(32); char next = realloc(p, 1024 1024); if (!next) { free(p); free(guard); return 1; } free(next); For successful movement, the raw event carries old_allocation_id, a new allocation_id and the recorded PID/sequence; the old lifetime ends at that event's sequence. In the final parser, heap(new_id).realloc_confidence is Definite only with matching creation event, predecessor creation, compatible same-PID lifetime boundaries and complete verified observed history. Partial/legacy evidence remains candidate or unavailable. src/trace_parser/validation.rs::realloc_link performs shared relationship checks; structural contradictions and cycles cannot become definite. - C: __wrap_malloc, __wrap_calloc, __wrap_realloc, __wrap_free, cte_emit_locked, cte_after_fork_child in c_runtime/alloc_tracker.c. - Rust: src/allocation_tracker.rs::{parse_event_line, EventTailer, HeapTimeline::ingest, verify_event_status}; src/trace.rs backfills snapshots and builds final state. - Parser: TraceStore::heap_events_for_allocation(id) uses a position index; ValidatedSemanticView::heap(id) qualifies identity and realloc separately. See schema fields(schema.htmlheap-records). WARNING: The wrapper does not intercept allocator calls made entirely inside unwrapped shared libraries, and the transport's terminal ACK verifies only observed PIDs plus the followed inferior. No absolute heap completeness or descendant coverage is promised.

title: Valgrind & sanitizers
summary: Independent diagnostics · Valgrind and sanitizers Level 1 · Intuition GDB shows what happened in the primary traced run. Valgrind and sanitizer runs can detect memory problems the primary trace does not prove, but they execute the
text: Independent diagnostics · Valgrind and sanitizers Level 1 · Intuition GDB shows what happened in the primary traced run. Valgrind and sanitizer runs can detect memory problems the primary trace does not prove, but they execute the program again. A similar address or source line across executions is not the same allocation. A diagnostic belongs to its own run; missing or truncated output is not a clean bill of health. {{diagram:metadata}} Level 2 · Stages and uncertainty Valgrind runs the compiled program independently and produces native XML. parse_valgrind_xml decodes complete error records, native summaries and leaks. If XML is truncated, recover_errors can retain complete <error elements while marking output incomplete and summary numbers unknown (observed_summary, nullable observed leak totals and parse error); a zero legacy total when the observed field is absent is not a measured zero. The runtime wrapper is passive in a Valgrind process so its table does not hide leaks as still-reachable objects. An ASan/UBSan-compiled executable is run separately when sanitizer_trigger selects never, on_crash, on_crash_or_valgrind_error (default) or always. Reports and StageResult distinguish skipped, timed out, failed and completed passes. An ASan diagnostic is attached to a primary crash only with supported source-site correlation; otherwise it stays an independent diagnostic_observed. A nonzero sanitizer exit with no diagnostic is inconclusive. Stage budget/cancellation may prevent analyses after a deadline; program execution_status is not overwritten by an unrelated Valgrind failure. Worked crash: useful prefix, separate completeness c // Source: fixtures/c/phase8r3_crash.c int observed_global = 123; int main(void) { (volatile int )0 = observed_global; return 0; } In a fresh audited run, this produced execution_status="crashed", a SIGSEGV crash report, 3 snapshots and 5 retained instruction attempts. coverage.complete_for_scope=true for the observed user-code interval, while heap_history.complete=false because the allocation tracker did not receive a normal terminal ACK. These are different dimensions: neither the crash nor heap partiality erases the captured stops, and a complete user-code scope does not make heap history complete. With a forced sanitizer pass, the separately run sanitizer also produced a diagnostic. Do not infer unrecorded writes or a complete process-tree history from the retained prefix. Source site is not identity src/valgrind.rs::correlate_with_allocations is a legacy-name helper that now ignores supplied primary allocation IDs; it may produce ID-free same-absolute-file/line candidates but never an exact cross-run allocation link. Imported legacy related_allocation_ids can remain in raw reports, yet TP-6 valgrind_error(index).primary_allocation_id is always None. See confidence contracts(parser-semantic.htmlindependent-diagnostics). Level 3 · Models and real failure path - src/valgrind.rs::{parse_valgrind_xml, recover_errors, correlate_with_allocations} and src/sanitizer.rs::{parse_sanitizer_output, matches_crash}. - src/trace.rs schedules passes and records stage_results; src/models.rs::{ValgrindReport, ValgrindError, SanitizerReport, CrashReport, StageResult} holds outputs. - ValidatedSemanticView::diagnostics() borrows the session reports; valgrind_error(index) provides a trace-local reference to an independent diagnostic. rust let diagnostics = validated.diagnostics(); if let Some(report) = diagnostics.valgrind { for index in 0..report.detailed_errors.len() { let item = validated.valgrind_error(index)?; assert!(item.primary_allocation_id.is_none()); } } The code assumes a previously defined validated view; see the runnable usage example(usage.htmllevel-3-load-and-validate). In the final Stage 1 audit, a fresh Valgrind fixture produced one native diagnostic and zero primary allocation links. Crash/forced-sanitizer samples each retained only the reports actually observed. A missing report is never a negative diagnosis. WARNING: A primary-run allocation ID found in an imported Valgrind raw field is not an authorized Stage 2 identity join. Do not use matching source, address, PID or name across executions as a substitute for same-execution event evidence.

title: Processes & event transport
summary: Process lifecycle, forks and event transport Level 1 · Intuition The debugger follows an inferior; the allocation wrapper can also write PID-labelled events from forked children. Those are different scopes. A child that forks, log
text: Process lifecycle, forks and event transport Level 1 · Intuition The debugger follows an inferior; the allocation wrapper can also write PID-labelled events from forked children. Those are different scopes. A child that forks, logs no allocation and exits silently may be invisible. “Every observed PID's events were verified” cannot mean “every descendant was discovered.” {{diagram:partial}} Level 2 · From wrapper file to scoped coverage c_runtime/alloc_tracker.c writes complete newline-terminated event lines to C_TRACE_EVENT_FILE with pid, per-process seq, event kind/ID/address and status. Each process has its own local IDs and sequence counter; the Rust timeline can widen IDs to (pid << 32) local_id when events from multiple PIDs are observed (subject to overflow checks). The journal can retain PID-local transport IDs even when the final JSON has widened IDs: these are different representations, not proof of cross-run equality. The wrapper registers a child-after-fork callback to reset its lock and counters; a terminal ACK is written only on normal shutdown. An abnormal _exit or crash can leave no child ACK. The tailer detects malformed/partial writes, gaps, missing ACKs and caps and marks history incomplete. heap_history.process_scope="verified_observed_pids_only" describes observed event PIDs plus the followed inferior. heap_history.complete tests this scope's verified sequence/transport/ACK/retention; unobserved_process_coverage="unknown" remains true even if one or several observed PIDs have valid ACKs. GDB retains stopped snapshots for the followed inferior, not guaranteed child instruction/stack snapshots. PID inequality alone is not a verified parent–child relationship for an arbitrary import. An incomplete observed child downgrades heap identity without fabricating a child snapshot. Worked fork cases The phase8dr_fork.c fixture produced in a fresh audit: observed mode has 6 heap events from two event PIDs and scoped completion; silent mode has 4 events from one observed PID and scoped completion despite a silent child; incomplete mode has 6 events from two PIDs with a missing child ACK and complete=false. All three have unobserved_process_coverage="unknown". Level 3 · Implementation and typed view - C: cte_after_fork_child, cte_write_all, cte_emit_locked, normal-exit status writer in c_runtime/alloc_tracker.c. - Rust: src/allocation_tracker.rs::{EventTailer, verify_event_status, HeapTimeline::global_id} and src/trace.rs assembly of HeapHistoryCoverage; src/supervisor.rs controls subprocess groups, cancellation, subreaper ownership and best-effort cgroup handling. - Parser: TraceStore::heap_process_scope() yields HeapProcessScope::Unknown, VerifiedObservedPidsOnly { observed_event_pids, followed_inferior_pid, observed_history_complete }, or Unsupported; validate_deep() verifies annotations against recorded events. process_coverage().unobserved_descendants remains unavailable on sound traces. json {"complete":true,"process_scope":"verified_observed_pids_only","unobserved_process_coverage":"unknown"} This is an illustrative subset of heap_history, not an all-process claim and not a complete JSON object for the model. Identity tables(schema.htmlidentity-domains) explain why per-PID sequences and global allocation IDs are not stops or event positions. WARNING: The engine is not a security sandbox. With no delegated cgroup, descendants escaping the owned group may evade tree-wide limits; neither RLIMIT_NPROC nor a global fork census is used.

title: Budgets, gaps & export
summary: Timeouts, budgets, coverage and export Level 1 · Intuition A finite tracing budget makes a useful partial recording rather than pretending missing data was observed. Different caps protect different things: journal bytes, JSON doc
text: Timeouts, budgets, coverage and export Level 1 · Intuition A finite tracing budget makes a useful partial recording rather than pretending missing data was observed. Different caps protect different things: journal bytes, JSON document size, debugger commands, snapshot reads, tool time and parser page size are not one universal memory limit. A crash, timeout or cap is an outcome; it does not automatically corrupt the records already captured. {{diagram:partial}} Level 2 · Budgets across stages supervisor::scope starts the global wall deadline before tool probes. Compiler, debugger and analysis deadlines are clamped to it. Every GDB command checks deadline and max_gdb_commands; an inferior stop-wait timeout and missing MI response have different diagnoses. SIGINT/SIGTERM request supervised cancellation and return useful partial JSON when possible; abrupt SIGKILL cannot finalize the journal. Subprocess groups and pipe drains are bounded; prlimit is installed on the stopped inferior (not GDB), optional delegated cgroups add best-effort process-tree limits, and neither provides a security sandbox. Limit Default Governs (not equivalent to RAM) ------:--- timeout_seconds 10 s Entire pipeline; per-stage limits clamp to it max_steps 1,000 Source/dual progression; separate from instruction cap max_instruction_events 100,000 Attempted instruction recording max_source_checkpoints 1,000 Selected source-state records max_trace_bytes 128 MiB JSONL journal byte accounting, not final JSON max_trace_memory_bytes 32 MiB Resident serialized-record accounting, not total Rust RSS max_json_export_bytes 128 MiB Each formatted final JSON document max_snapshot_memory_bytes 1 MiB Budget of captured bytes at a checkpoint max_gdb_commands 1,000,000 MI queries and control commands MAX_CONSUMER_PAGE 128 Trace Parser TP-7 results in a single request The recorder preserves coverage.scope, complete_for_scope, truncation_reasons, stop_model and trace_gaps with attempted-position boundaries. Disassembly/AST/heap histories have their own partiality. storage.finalized means journal collection closed, not successful program completion. --journal-only can omit resident instruction arrays; journal records can be read sequentially, but cannot be converted into a complete TraceStore without final JSON. Measured counterexample to conflated caps The final audit set --max-trace-bytes 2048: the JSONL journal was 1,961 bytes, but separately exported JSON was 22,883 bytes and correctly marked partial. A second run with --max-json-export-bytes 8192 exited with max_json_export_bytes exceeded and wrote no JSON. Neither test establishes a peak process-RAM limit. See parser ingestion limits(parser-ingestion.htmllevel-2-architecture-and-compatibility). Level 3 · Enforcement sites and results - src/resource_limits.rs::{ExecutionLimits::validate, limit_stopped_inferior, CgroupGuard}; src/supervisor.rs::{scope, stage_deadline, request_cancel}. - src/recorder.rs::{Recorder::truncate, Recorder::checkpoint, Recorder::event} and src/storage.rs::{Journal::append, Journal::finalize, recover} distinguish retained records from journal and total attempts; src/models.rs::RecordingData holds the serialized result. - src/json_export.rs::{preflight, export_json_cancellable} bounds each emitted JSON document without first assembling a giant output string. This does not bound the already assembled DebugSessionTrace or parser RSS. sh target/release/c-trace-engine fixtures/c/infinite_loop.c \ --trace-mode dual --max-steps 60 --timeout 35 \ --no-pretty --output /tmp/visual-c-limit.json A capped trace can have execution_status=step_limit_reached, retained events, gaps and coverage.complete_for_scope=false. Consumers should read validation findings(parser-validation.html) and confidence(parser-semantic.html), not interpret compiled_successfully=true as complete execution. WARNING: Trace Parser input cap defaults to 512 MiB; this prevents oversized input buffering but does not make deserialization/trace assembly constant-memory. The 128-record page bound constrains query outputs, not the whole trace.

title: Trace data model
summary: DebugSessionTrace · the recorded data model Level 1 · Intuition A trace is not a video of a program. It is a set of timestamped/stopped observations, bounded attempts and gaps, heap telemetry, optional static metadata and diagnost
text: DebugSessionTrace · the recorded data model Level 1 · Intuition A trace is not a video of a program. It is a set of timestamped/stopped observations, bounded attempts and gaps, heap telemetry, optional static metadata and diagnostics. Links between them use different identity domains. Preserving absent evidence is just as important as preserving a successful read. {{diagram:records}} Level 2 · Record relationships DebugSessionTrace flattens RecordingData into the top-level JSON object (serde(flatten)), while keeping snapshots, heap_events, heap_state, stage results, compilation diagnostics, optional reports and static metadata alongside it. recording.instruction_events in Rust appears as top-level instruction_events in JSON. source_checkpoints stores indices into snapshots rather than cloned snapshots. disassembly_table contains unique address/text table entries; instruction events refer by instruction_id, while repeated dynamic visits retain separate event positions. trace_gaps record unknown intervals at attempted positions, not fake events. allocation_lifetimes, final heap_state and chronological heap_events are distinct views of observed heap activity. coverage (user-code instruction scope), heap_history (verified observed-PID events), storage and stage_results are independent dimensions. Events, gaps and checkpoints - snapshotsi.step_index=i: captured checkpoint position. snapshotsi.observation.stop_id: processed debugger stop counter; may have holes. instruction_position: number of attempts preceding it. - instruction_eventsj.event_id: ordered attempted instruction ID; optional checkpoint_id references a recent snapshot, not an exact temporal join. stop_id_before/after refer to debugger observations. - trace_gapsk.instruction_position is a boundary where instructions were not captured; its unknown instruction count is never guessed. Variables, bytes and heap VariableInfo.read_status, bytes_status and memory_evidence describe distinct observations. Pointer address is storage and points_to is the pointee. HeapEvent.sequence is per-PID, not event-vector position. HeapBlockInfo.observed_at_stop timestamps heap byte reads; a freed final block may retain historical bytes. AllocationLifetime has an allocation sequence and optional free sequence; a successful realloc can link old and new lifetime IDs. The schema does not create pointer origin from address equality. Level 3 · Actual schema excerpt and paths rust // Reduced field excerpt from src/models.rs; other fields omitted. pub struct DebugSessionTrace { pub schema_version: u32, pub snapshots: Vec<ExecutionSnapshot, pub heap_events: Vec<HeapEvent, pub heap_state: Vec<HeapBlockInfo, pub execution_status: ExecutionStatus, pub stage_results: StageResults, // serde(flatten) pub recording: RecordingData, } Illustrative reduced excerpt, not a copy/paste Rust definition or complete JSON: DebugSessionTrace also contains typed execution_limits, execution, compilation results, optional metadata and reports, usage and notes. For the actual declaration, see src/models.rs::DebugSessionTrace and schema reference(schema.html). json {"schema_version":2,"execution_status":"step_limit_reached","instruction_count":203,"coverage":{"scope":"user_code","complete_for_scope":false,"truncation_reasons":"max_steps"}} This is an illustrative partial JSON projection: no unspecified keys are implied, and a real trace's truncation-reason list may include additional causes. The importer requires the full model, not this excerpt. schema_version is 2 for supported V2.1/V2.2 documents; a missing marker defaults to 2, but unknown old execution_limits fields can still make pre-V2.1 files fail to deserialize. See TP-1 compatibility(parser-ingestion.htmllevel-2-architecture-and-compatibility). NOTE: The wire model records uncertainty as Option/nullable values and explicit status fields. Never rewrite a missing stop_id_after, unloaded AST registry or unreadable bytes to a successful observation. Find identity semantics in the reference dictionary(schema.htmlidentity-domains).

title: TP-1 · Load & compatibility
summary: TP-1 · Loading traces without inventing data Level 1 · Intuition The Trace Parser reads the engine's finished JSON exactly once and makes a single immutable TraceStore available to multiple readers. Successful parsing means schema
text: TP-1 · Loading traces without inventing data Level 1 · Intuition The Trace Parser reads the engine's finished JSON exactly once and makes a single immutable TraceStore available to multiple readers. Successful parsing means schema-compatible, not “all records are internally consistent” and not “the program ran to completion.” Deep validation is an explicit separate step. {{diagram:ownership}} Level 2 · Architecture and compatibility TraceStore::open(path, options) checks file size and reads at most max_bytes + 1, then content-detects a JSON document or journal. from_reader and from_json_bytes support byte inputs; from_trace adopts an already decoded model and applies only the schema-version gate. TraceLoadOptions defaults to a 512 MiB input cap and 2,000,000 JSONL records, rejecting larger inputs rather than silently truncating them. The loader does not retain original JSON text. TraceStore::assemble builds one Arc<DebugSessionTrace and one Arc<TraceIndexes; cheap clones share both. The wire schema version is 2; the supported V2.1 examples (normal, loop, heap, crash, dual, bounded infinite) load, including optional missing metadata. A missing schema marker defaults to 2 per Serde model. The four older pre-V2.1 examples/v2_.json files with removed max_register_snapshot_bytes do not deserialize; do not advertise support for all historical schema-2 payloads. Wrong schema, invalid UTF-8, malformed JSON and over-limit input produce typed errors. Crash/timeout/step-limit are valid trace outcomes, not parser failures. JSONL is not a TraceStore parse_journal, parse_journal_bytes and parse_journal_reader decode ordered typed records (configuration, checkpoint, allocation, gap, disassembly, instruction, finalized) with per-kind counts and torn-tail/finalization status. An incomplete final line can be recognized, but a complete malformed line fails. Final heap state, reports and other session-end fields are not in JSONL; TraceStore::open refuses to reconstruct a full trace from it. See storage and caps(engine-limits.html). Level 3 · Implementation and API rust use c_trace_engine::trace_parser::{TraceLoadOptions, TraceStore}; fn main() - Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error { let store = TraceStore::open("examples/v21_dual.json", TraceLoadOptions::default())?; assert_eq!(store.trace().schema_version, 2); let validated = store.validated_semantic(); // opt-in; not part of open() if !validated.report().is_structurally_sound() { eprintln!("import has contradictory record relationships"); } Ok(()) } The snippet is executable as a Rust example in this crate (adjust the path if run elsewhere); for a larger end-to-end query see Practical usage(usage.htmllevel-3-load-and-validate). Actual TraceStore methods: open, from_reader, from_json_bytes, from_trace, trace, shared, source, validate_deep. src/trace_parser/{mod,json,journal,error}.rs implement ingestion; TraceParseError covers malformed input, unsupported schema, journal-only input and limits. src/trace_parser/indexes.rs eagerly builds positions after successful decoding. open preserves file path/byte length in a small TraceSourceMetadata descriptor. WARNING: Neither schema compatibility nor heap_process_scope() on raw input certifies a claimed relationship. For imported/untrusted data, inspect validated.report() and the confidence/coverage of each relationship before presenting it as fact.

title: TP-2 · Position indexes
summary: TP-2 · Compact, position-only indexes Level 1 · Intuition A large trace repeats instruction addresses and source lines thousands of times. Scanning every event for each question would waste time; copying every record into lookup t
text: TP-2 · Compact, position-only indexes Level 1 · Intuition A large trace repeats instruction addresses and source lines thousands of times. Scanning every event for each question would waste time; copying every record into lookup tables would waste memory. TP-2 builds keys → integer positions once and borrows original records when queried. It does not create an address→allocation provenance index. {{diagram:ownership}} Level 2 · What is indexed TraceIndexes::build eagerly constructs the index during TraceStore::assemble. ExecutionsIndex groups all retained event positions for each disassembly table ID using contiguous offset arrays. SourceIndex interns complete file paths and exact (file,line) keys, mapping to static instruction IDs and all dynamic event positions; the reverse mapping retrieves source positions for a disassembled instruction. AllocationIndex maps allocation ID to event positions, final state position and lifetime position. MetadataIndex maps trace-local DWARF/AST IDs and source/heap-call candidate IDs to registry positions. Only positions/keys are retained; no large memory bytes, snapshots or events are cloned into indexes. Direct vector access needs no index for snapshot index or event_id. GDB stop IDs and checkpoint event runs use verified monotonic ordering and binary searches, not a stop hash map. Heap-event intervals use neighboring retained snapshots' cumulative heap_event_count boundaries; skipped stops make timing coarser, not an exact join. Imported broken order yields OrderingViolation rather than an unreliable binary-search result. No source-basename equivalence and no address-to-lifetime join are cached. Mini example Disassembly instruction 12 may occur at instruction_events positions 5, 21, 36. The index contains three u32 positions, not three copies of the event or one merged “executed once” record. instruction_execution_positions(12) returns that slice; instruction_executions(12) borrows canonical event records at each position. instruction_id=12 is not event 12. Level 3 · Source and query contracts - src/trace_parser/indexes.rs::{TraceIndexes, ExecutionsIndex, SourceIndex, AllocationIndex, MetadataIndex, OrderingFacts}. - TraceStore::{instruction_event, instruction_range, events_at_checkpoint, snapshot_at_stop, instruction_executions, executed_events_for_source, heap_events_for_allocation, allocation_lifetime} in src/trace_parser/mod.rs. rust let positions: &u32 = store.heap_event_positions_for_allocation(allocation_id); for &position in positions { let heap_event = &store.heap_events()position as usize; assert_eq!(heap_event.allocation_id, allocation_id); } This excerpt assumes store and allocation_id are defined. It visits recorded heap-event positions without confusing them with event_id, stop IDs or allocation IDs; the executable usage sample(usage.htmlcheckpoints-and-paging) also handles empty traces and paginates. TraceIndexes::estimated_bytes() is a rough logical estimate of index structures, not process RSS. In the Stage 1 audit the 900-snapshot/3,143-instruction trace had ~28,369 estimated index bytes, ~1.13 ms median index build and ~17 MiB parser-process RSS after indexing (process includes trace, runtime and buffers; workload-specific). NOTE: A valid empty source/heap lookup means “no matching recorded item”; it is not a statement that nothing happened in a gap, another process or an uninstrumented library.

title: TP-3 · Borrowed views
summary: TP-3 · Borrowed views and EvidenceRef Level 1 · Intuition One large immutable trace should have many lightweight readers, not many copies. A view is a borrowed window into canonical records; an EvidenceRef is a trace-scoped citati
text: TP-3 · Borrowed views and EvidenceRef Level 1 · Intuition One large immutable trace should have many lightweight readers, not many copies. A view is a borrowed window into canonical records; an EvidenceRef is a trace-scoped citation that can later be resolved against that same recording. Equal numeric indices in two independent traces do not refer to the same execution. {{diagram:ownership}} Level 2 · Ownership and lifecycle TraceStore owns Arc<DebugSessionTrace and Arc<TraceIndexes; cloning the store cheaply shares both. raw() exposes recorded evidence, while semantic_input() builds CheckpointContext from a snapshot index or a source_checkpoints position and offers borrowed stack, locals, caller frames, globals, live heap and metadata. A context's events_at_checkpoint() finds explicit checkpoint tags; heap_events_in_snapshot_interval() uses adjacent retained cumulative counters. A missing stop/source association returns Unavailable rather than creating a fake stop. EvidenceLocation names a collection and position, e.g. Snapshot(3), SnapshotVariable { snapshot:3, variable:1 }, HeapEvent(7), AllocationLifetime(2), CrashReport, or ValgrindError(0). EvidenceRef also carries a weak Arc trace identity. resolve_evidence checks identity first: a cloned store resolves the reference; an independent reload of equal JSON rejects it as ForeignTrace. The reference is not a portable serialized ID or a cached ownership graph. Worked citation A variable on the top frame of snapshot 3 may be observed with snapshot.context.variable_evidence(1)?. Resolving that reference returns the same canonical VariableInfo as store.trace().snapshots3.variables1. A later stop with a local of the same name is not substituted. See TP-6 variable confidence(parser-semantic.htmlpointer-and-memory-confidence). Level 3 · APIs and errors rust use c_trace_engine::trace_parser::{EvidenceLocation, TraceStore}; let store = TraceStore::open("examples/v21_dual.json", Default::default())?; let cite = store.evidence_ref(EvidenceLocation::Snapshot(0))?; let same_run = store.resolve_evidence(&cite)?; // borrows original record let _ = (cite.location(), same_run); The snippet is a body excerpt (wrap it in fn main() - Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error); see Practical usage(usage.htmllevel-3-load-and-validate) for a standalone example. Implementation: src/trace_parser/{views,evidence}.rs; TraceStore::raw, semantic_input, evidence_ref, resolve_evidence. A QueryError distinguishes OutOfRange, InvalidRange, LimitExceeded, InvalidReference, ForeignTrace, Unavailable and OrderingViolation. No caller should turn an error into “zero evidence.” NOTE: A borrowed CheckpointContext cannot outlive its store. Keeping a separate Arc<DebugSessionTrace alive is possible with shared(), but a different TraceStore::open still has a different trace identity even with byte-identical contents.

title: TP-5 · Deep validation
summary: TP-5 · Deep structural validation Level 1 · Intuition A JSON file can have the right shape and still contradict itself. TP-5's opt-in deep validation checks cross-record relationships. It distinguishes a corrupt link from a legiti
text: TP-5 · Deep structural validation Level 1 · Intuition A JSON file can have the right shape and still contradict itself. TP-5's opt-in deep validation checks cross-record relationships. It distinguishes a corrupt link from a legitimate missing observation: a crashed or truncated program can yield a structurally sound but incomplete trace. {{diagram:confidence}} Level 2 · Architecture validate_deep() aggregates ValidationFinding { severity, code, detail, location, occurrences } in a ValidationReport. Its four severities are StructuralCorruption, PartialCoverage, UnavailableEvidence, OptionalAbsence. is_structurally_sound() means no structural finding—not complete instruction, process, byte or diagnostic coverage. is_partial() concerns only partial findings. TP-6 creates this report once; it downgrades all semantic confidence to Contradictory when the report is unsound, while retaining raw records for investigation. The pass reuses processor::validate() and checks event/disassembly/checkpoint references, event/stop ordering, snapshot indices, source-checkpoint bounds, gaps and attempted counts, duplicate heap/lifetime/metadata identities, pointer status vs claimed heap IDs, heap PID/history annotations, static links and diagnostic/coverage coherence. address_only with a definite allocation ID is contradictory even if a block contains that address. A false complete_all_processes annotation is unsupported. Legacy missing provenance or process scope is not synthesized; it is unavailable/unknown. Realloc link verification A block's realloc_from_id is not enough. realloc_link compares indexed creation events of both new and predecessor identities with lifetimes: Reallocated must name the exact old ID; PID, order, allocation/free sequence and direction must agree. Self-links, cycles and explicitly conflicting events are structural contradictions even if history is partial. Missing corroboration receives UnavailableEvidence; an observed link in incomplete scope cannot become definite. glibc's realloc(ptr,0) terminal-free same-ID/null-address/zero-size event ends a lifetime but is not new lifetime creation. No address equality decides a predecessor. Heap lifetimes(engine-heap.html) explains the source events. Level 3 · Report and import example rust let store = TraceStore::open(path, TraceLoadOptions::default())?; let report = store.validate_deep(); // explicit; not called by TraceStore::open for finding in report.findings() { eprintln!("{} at {}: {}", finding.code, finding.location, finding.detail); } if report.is_partial() { / retain the usable prefix, display missing scope / } This is a body excerpt; use the executable sample(usage.htmllevel-3-load-and-validate) for imports. src/trace_parser/validation.rs::{validate_deep, validate_heap, validate_heap_process_coverage, validate_pointer_reference, realloc_link} implements checks. The resulting ValidationReport borrows no input JSON and aggregates occurrences by code; first_location_findings() on a TP-7 checkpoint is not a completeness proof for that checkpoint. TraceStore::from_trace intentionally remains schema-only. Example findings Code Class Correct response --------- REALLOC_LINK_CONTRADICTORY Structural Preserve raw import for investigation; never claim definite predecessor POINTER_HEAP_PROVENANCE_CONTRADICTORY Structural Do not promote an address-only candidate HEAP_PROCESS_COVERAGE_UNSUPPORTED Structural Reject claimed all-descendant completeness HEAP_HISTORY_INCOMPLETE Partial Preserve observed events; downgrade history-dependent confidence REALLOC_LINK_UNVERIFIED Unavailable Do not infer missing event/lifetime data SANITIZER_REPORT_UNRECORDED Optional Absent report is not proof of no bug WARNING: Trusting successful deserialization—or a raw heap_history.complete field without checking its scope and report—is a false-certainty bug. The F01 regression(../trace-parser-v2.2-repair-f01.md) permanently checks the repaired realloc relationship.

title: TP-6 · Evidence confidence
summary: TP-6 · Validated semantic evidence Level 1 · Intuition “Definite” must answer which relationship, in what scope. A readable byte can be a definite capture without a definite C initialization. A pointer can definitely contain an ad
text: TP-6 · Validated semantic evidence Level 1 · Intuition “Definite” must answer which relationship, in what scope. A readable byte can be a definite capture without a definite C initialization. A pointer can definitely contain an address without a definite allocation origin. TP-6 packages borrowed evidence with per-relationship confidence; it is not the future C Semantic Engine. {{diagram:confidence}} Level 2 · The confidence model Call TraceStore::validated_semantic() once per analysis session; it holds one ValidationReport and borrows the immutable store. EvidenceConfidence has five states: Definite (verified observation/relationship in stated scope), Candidate (plausible but unproved), Ambiguous (multiple compatible readings), Unavailable (no sufficient evidence), and Contradictory (a rejected structural relationship). An unsound report conservatively makes semantic query confidence contradictory globally; raw evidence is still inspectable. This model is separate from ExecutionStatus, scope liveness, byte readability, initialization and process coverage. Pointer and memory confidence variable(&EvidenceRef) borrows local/global/caller VariableInfo, optional static metadata, value confidence and MemoryEvidenceView. A PointerEvidence.address_candidate is a numeric containment candidate, not provenance; definitive_allocation is always None under present V2.2 statuses. address_only, known freed, reused/ambiguous and incomplete history remain candidate, ambiguous or unavailable as appropriate. variable_target(&VariableEvidence) resolves a recorded variable identity only within the same stop (and rejects foreign refs); duplicate identities remain ambiguous. Readable valid_range certifies captured bytes in one historical observation, never C initialization or a future heap block's contents. Identity and source relationships heap(id) borrows block, lifetime, old ID, old lifetime and event iterator. Identity confidence can be definite only in a verified complete observed-PID history; corroborated realloc confidence additionally requires exact event/lifetime predecessor agreement. Incomplete/legacy scope downgrades a supported link to candidate. source_expression(id) borrows optional AST and recorded heap-call candidates; execution_confidence remains unavailable. A compatible source line is not a dynamic execution link. Independent diagnostics diagnostics() borrows compile, stage, crash, sanitizer and Valgrind records. valgrind_error(index) exposes source-site candidate confidence, but primary_allocation_id is always None, including for legacy imported raw IDs. process_coverage().unobserved_descendants stays unavailable on sound traces; heap_history.complete is not a descendant census. execution() reports attempted vs retained counts, gaps and engine-declared scope independently. Level 3 · The relevant implementation - src/trace_parser/semantic.rs::{ValidatedSemanticView, EvidenceConfidence, VariableEvidence, MemoryEvidenceView, PointerEvidence, HeapEvidence, SourceExpressionEvidence, ExecutionEvidence, ProcessCoverageEvidence}. - TraceStore::validated_semantic calls self.validate_deep() once. SemanticInputView::validated() offers the same path. self.qualify downgrades on structural unsoundness without mutating source records. - heap(id) uses TP-2's per-allocation event positions and the shared validation::realloc_link classifier. source_expression(id) uses TP-2 metadata candidate/ambiguity positions; no global pointer graph or synthetic execution interpreter is stored. rust let view = store.validated_semantic(); if !view.report().is_structurally_sound() { eprintln!("Structural contradiction; do not present definite links"); } let evidence = view.heap(allocation_id); let _ = (evidence.identity_confidence, evidence.realloc_confidence, evidence.old_id, evidence.events()); This excerpt assumes store and allocation_id; the full runnable walkthrough(usage.htmllevel-3-load-and-validate) covers imports. old_id is raw recorded data and not itself a certified edge; inspect realloc_confidence. A heap-event interval's TP-7 allocation(&view) inherits this same confidence rather than silently upgrading a candidate. WARNING: “Definite” is scoped to the specifically named observation or relationship. It does not imply a complete primary execution, a complete process tree, initialized bytes or that independent diagnostics belong to the primary run.

title: TP-7 · Bounded queries
summary: TP-7 · Checkpoint composition and bounded pages Level 1 · Intuition A user-facing query often wants several related things at one stop: variables, instruction events, heap events, gaps and optional diagnostics. TP-7 composes exist
text: TP-7 · Checkpoint composition and bounded pages Level 1 · Intuition A user-facing query often wants several related things at one stop: variables, instruction events, heap events, gaps and optional diagnostics. TP-7 composes existing TP-6 evidence around a checkpoint without copying a trace or inventing a second evidence-ID system. Every page is explicitly limited to 128 records: request the next range to continue. {{diagram:consumer}} Level 2 · What a summary means checkpoint_summary(index) borrows one CheckpointEvidence, its trace-scoped snapshot EvidenceRef, and the validated view. snapshot_index, stop_id, attempted_instruction_position, recorded PID and source line are distinct, not convertible integers. variables_page(Local Global Caller(position), range) returns qualified TP-6 variable views. caller_frame(position) and frame_activation(id) use the recorded activation within that same stop. instruction_events_page(range) returns events explicitly tagged with this checkpoint ID; the tag is definite, not exact same-stop causality. heap_interval_page(range) groups events by adjacent retained snapshots' cumulative heap counts, with only Candidate interval timing. gaps_in_attempted_window(range) cites attempted-position windows, not causal attribution to one stop. source_expressions_page(range) scans optional AST by exact recorded file/span and returns static candidates, not execution proof. Session-wide coverage(), session_diagnostics(), session_report_refs(), valgrind_errors_page() and first_location_findings() stay separate from event cause. A report recorded in a session need not have happened at this checkpoint; “first validation finding here” is not a certificate of local completeness. heap_events_page(&allocation_ref, range) rejects foreign trace references before using numeric IDs. HeapIntervalEvidence::allocation(&validated) inherits TP-6 realloc confidence. Level 3 · Real signatures and bounded traversal rust // Excerpt for a previously constructed view: ValidatedSemanticView. let stop = view.checkpoint_summary(0)?; let len = stop.checkpoint.context.variables().len(); for start in (0..len).step_by(128) { let end = (start + 128).min(len); for item in stop.variables_page(VariableScope::Local, start..end)? { let variable = item?; // borrowed VariableInfo + confidence + EvidenceRef let _ = (variable.info.name.as_str(), variable.value_confidence); } } This excerpt assumes VariableScope is imported and a nonempty trace (use the complete runnable example(usage.htmlcheckpoints-and-paging) for zero-snapshot handling). MAX_CONSUMER_PAGE=128 in src/trace_parser/consumer.rs governs each half-open Range<usize; empty pages are valid. Reversed or past-end ranges return InvalidRange; width 129 returns LimitExceeded without dropping rows. src/trace_parser/indexes.rs supplies event/allocation positions, views.rs supplies borrowed checkpoint context, and semantic.rs supplies unchanged TP-6 confidence. Cost and ordering Stop/event/gap windows use verified order and binary search. Heap interval pagination uses canonical event slices and counters; AST source spans are scanned on demand within bounded registry size. Per-page iteration borrows existing records; it does not build an unbounded output array. The audit exercised 3,143 real retained instructions across 900 checkpoints; separate permanent tests exercise 300 events and 1,024 variables across multiple ≤128 pages. The large real trace does not prove 128 events at a single real checkpoint. See performance(handoff.htmlperformance-not-a-guarantee). NOTE: Keep the page's borrowed lifetime bounded by its ValidatedSemanticView; do not collect an unbounded Vec just because the API makes small pages cheap. When evidence is Unavailable, handle it explicitly rather than displaying an empty success state.

title: Worked API walkthrough
summary: Practical usage · from C file to borrowed evidence Level 1 · Intuition Run the engine to obtain a JSON document, then parse that document and check its deep-validation report before asking what happened at a checkpoint. One parser
text: Practical usage · from C file to borrowed evidence Level 1 · Intuition Run the engine to obtain a JSON document, then parse that document and check its deep-validation report before asking what happened at a checkpoint. One parser store can serve many readers. Observations stay historical; a missing diagnosis or event is not a proven absence. {{diagram:consumer}} Level 2 · Run a recording From the repository root on the supported Linux toolchain: sh cargo build --release target/release/c-trace-engine fixtures/c/phase8b_defined.c \ --trace-mode dual --max-steps 350 --timeout 50 \ --clang-ast --sanitizer-trigger never \ --journal /tmp/visual-c-session.jsonl \ --no-pretty --output /tmp/visual-c-session.json python3 -m json.tool /tmp/visual-c-session.json /tmp/visual-c-readable.json GCC/GDB must be installed; Clang is optional for this command's --clang-ast pass (without it, remove the flag). Valgrind may run as an independent stage if available; --sanitizer-trigger never disables the separate sanitizer run. Do not pass -- before engine options; only program arguments follow --. The engine writes one full JSON document to --output; JSONL can be parsed for records but not loaded as a complete TraceStore. Journals are never overwritten: choose a fresh --journal path for each repeat run (or remove your previous audit-owned temporary file first). See compilation(engine-build.html), deadline policy(engine-limits.html) and the input schema(parser-ingestion.html). A real captured pointer, carefully read The audited phase8b_defined.c trace's frame-0 heap variable at snapshot 4 recorded points_to="0x705010" and the following abridged, exact-field pointer target: json {"kind":"heap","allocation_id":null,"base_address":"0x705010","offset_bytes":0,"active":true,"within_extent":true,"variable_identity":null,"address_match_allocation_id":1,"provenance_status":"address_only"} The raw event at sequence 1 created allocation ID 1 at 0x705010. Matching the numeric address did not certify the pointer's provenance: allocation_id stayed null and the evidence layer's definitive_allocation remains None. Addresses/PIDs can change in new runs; do not hardcode these values. At the same run's checkpoint line 15, snapshot 36 / GDB stop 119 / attempted instruction position 116 are different identifiers; sum displayed "10" with bytes "0a000000". Level 3 · Load and validate The following is a complete Rust example body for examples/stage1_docs_consumer.rs; it uses only public APIs. Save it there and run cargo run --example stage1_docs_consumer -- /tmp/visual-c-session.json (or use the checked-in larger audit consumer cargo run --release --example stage1_public_consumer_audit -- /tmp/visual-c-session.json). rust use c_trace_engine::trace_parser::{ EvidenceLocation, TraceLoadOptions, TraceStore, VariableScope, MAX_CONSUMER_PAGE, }; fn main() - Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error { let path = std::env::args().nth(1).ok_or("provide trace JSON path")?; let store = TraceStore::open(&path, TraceLoadOptions::default())?; let view = store.validated_semantic(); // one deep validation pass for finding in view.report().findings() { eprintln!("{}: {} ({})", finding.severity.label(), finding.code, finding.location); } if !view.report().is_structurally_sound() { return Err("contradictory imported relationships; inspect raw evidence".into()); } println!("status={:?} partial={}", view.execution().status, view.report().is_partial()); for index in 0..store.trace().snapshots.len() { let stop = view.checkpoint_summary(index)?; assert_eq!(stop.reference.location(), EvidenceLocation::Snapshot(index)); let locals = stop.checkpoint.context.variables().len(); for start in (0..locals).step_by(MAX_CONSUMER_PAGE) { let end = (start + MAX_CONSUMER_PAGE).min(locals); for entry in stop.variables_page(VariableScope::Local, start..end)? { let var = entry?; println!("{}: {:?}", var.info.name, var.value_confidence); if let Some(ptr) = &var.pointer { println!("address candidate={:?}; provenance={:?}", ptr.address_candidate, ptr.definitive_allocation); } } } } let process = view.process_coverage(); println!("observed scope={:?}; descendants={:?}", process.scope, process.unobserved_descendants); Ok(()) } Checkpoints and paging This example iterates all retained checkpoints and requests half-open pages of ≤128 locals. It never suppresses a page error or promotes address containment to provenance. Other page lengths come from the actual context (globals(), caller_frames()), event slice (events_at_checkpoint()?) or allocation-position index (heap_event_positions_for_allocation(id)); always request subsequent ranges explicitly. Use view.heap_reference(&ref) for trace-scoped heap evidence, view.diagnostics() for independent reports, and CheckpointSummary(parser-consumer.html) for per-stop composition. The API reference(api.html) details the signatures. Troubleshooting Symptom What to check ------ CompileFailed, no snapshots compile_errors, stage_results.compiler and tool versions; a syntax error is not an empty successful run ForeignTrace Do not pass EvidenceRef from a separately loaded JSON, even if bytes are identical Unavailable AST/bytes Was --clang-ast enabled? Was memory readable and within its budget? Unknown is not zero StepLimitReached / missing heap ACK Consult coverage, gaps, heap history, stage results and partial findings InvalidRange / LimitExceeded Use start..end with end≤len and end-start≤128; do not truncate silently REALLOC_LINK_CONTRADICTORY Imported predecessor disagrees with event/lifetime; inspect verification rules(parser-validation.htmlrealloc-link-verification) NOTE: A structurally sound report can still be partial or missing optional evidence. Treat the report and each per-relationship confidence as different questions.

summary: Public API reference · Trace Engine and Parser Level 1 · Intuition The engine creates a DebugSessionTrace from C source; the parser makes that finished recording navigable. Loading, deep validation and semantic confidence are thre
text: Public API reference · Trace Engine and Parser Level 1 · Intuition The engine creates a DebugSessionTrace from C source; the parser makes that finished recording navigable. Loading, deep validation and semantic confidence are three separate operations. Use trace-scoped references for identity, explicit bounded pages for display, and the report for import integrity. {{diagram:handoff}} Level 2 · Ownership and query path TraceConfig/BuildConfig → async trace_program → JSON export; then TraceStore::open → Arc<DebugSessionTrace + Arc<TraceIndexes → validated_semantic() → borrowed CheckpointSummary/EvidenceRef. Cloning a store shares owners; constructing an independent store changes reference identity. All queries borrow canonical records; source_expression(id) and bare heap(id) are trace-local string/numeric lookups, not portable identity tokens. A whole-trace ValidationReport is created once per validated view; pages do not revalidate. Level 3 · Signatures and contracts Record and load Public item (path) Result / contract ------ trace_program(config: TraceConfig) - Result<DebugSessionTrace (src/trace.rs, async) Runs supervised engine; failure trace is still a structured result when possible TraceStore::open(path: impl AsRef<Path, options: TraceLoadOptions) - Result<Self Schema-2 JSON file; 512 MiB default input cap TraceStore::from_json_bytes(bytes: &u8, options: TraceLoadOptions) - Result<Self Explicit one JSON document TraceStore::from_reader(reader: impl Read, options: TraceLoadOptions) - Result<Self Bounded stream read TraceStore::from_trace(trace: DebugSessionTrace) - Result<Self Schema-only gate; does not run validate_deep parse_journal(path, options) - Result<JournalTrace Ordered JSONL records only, no reconstructed TraceStore store.trace() - &DebugSessionTrace, store.shared() - Arc<DebugSessionTrace Canonical immutable owner; clone shares indexes Raw and referenced navigation Public item Use ------ store.snapshot(index), instruction_event(index), instruction_range(range) Original position/half-open borrowed records; raw TP-2 ranges are not TP-7 pages store.events_at_checkpoint(snapshot_index), snapshot_at_stop(stop_id) Explicit tag run and verified-order stop lookup; stop ID is not snapshot index store.instruction_executions(instruction_id), executed_events_for_source(file,line) Preserve repeated dynamic visits; exact recorded source strings store.heap_events_for_allocation(id), heap_block(id), allocation_lifetime(id) Trace-local allocation ID, not address or event position store.raw(), store.semantic_input().checkpoint_context(index) Borrowed canonical source and checkpoint context store.evidence_ref(location), store.resolve_evidence(&reference) Trace-scoped EvidenceRef; foreign store → ForeignTrace Validation and qualified evidence Public item Contract ------ store.validate_deep() - ValidationReport Opt-in structural, partial, unavailable and optional findings store.validated_semantic() - ValidatedSemanticView<'_ Once-deep-validated borrower; view.report() must be inspected view.variable(&EvidenceRef), view.variable_target(&VariableEvidence) Variable/byte/pointer and same-stop variable-identity relationship view.heap(id), view.heap_reference(&EvidenceRef) Identity and separate realloc predecessor confidence view.source_expression(id) Static metadata and call candidates; not execution view.checkpoint(index), view.execution(), view.process_coverage() Stop and independent execution/process dimensions view.diagnostics(), view.valgrind_error(index) Independent reports; never a primary-run Valgrind allocation ID TP-7 pages (all range: Range<usize are half-open) Public item Returned evidence ------ view.checkpoint_summary(index) Borrowed CheckpointSummary<'_, '_ and snapshot reference stop.variables_page(VariableScope::{Local, Global, Caller(position)}, range) TP-6 variable confidence; caller position is not GDB level stop.instruction_events_page(range), stop.heap_interval_page(range) Explicit tag / candidate interval; not exact event cause stop.gaps_in_attempted_window(range), stop.source_expressions_page(range) Position-window gaps / optional static syntax stop.caller_frame(position), stop.frame_activation(id) Same-snapshot activation; missing association is not guessed view.heap_events_page(&EvidenceRef, range), view.valgrind_errors_page(range) Trace-scoped allocation event rows / independent diagnostics stop.coverage(), stop.session_diagnostics(), stop.first_location_findings() Distinct scope, session reports and finding's first location All TP-7 page widths are ≤ MAX_CONSUMER_PAGE (128); an oversize request returns QueryError::LimitExceeded, not a truncated iterator. Raw TraceStore::instruction_range has its separate slice API; do not misstate the TP-7 bound as a universal input/trace-size cap. See pagination implementation(parser-consumer.htmllevel-3-real-signatures-and-bounded-traversal) and the runnable example(usage.htmllevel-3-load-and-validate). NOTE: Type annotations above summarize the public methods; some pages return impl Iterator<Item=QueryResult<_ rather than a copied vector. Consult the named Rust source for complete generic and lifetime parameters.
