text: Schema v2 and identity reference Level 1 · Intuition A source line, stopped PC, snapshot position, instruction attempt, allocation lifetime and process address are different kinds of information. Mixing their integers creates convincing but false explanations. The model deliberately records explicit references, nullable fields, scopes and gaps so readers can say what was observed and what remains unknown. {{diagram:records}} Level 2 · Top-level JSON The Rust type is src/models.rs::DebugSessionTrace; RecordingData is serde(flatten) into JSON. Typical top-level fields: schema_version=2, compiled_successfully, compile_errors, snapshots, heap_events, heap_state, allocation_lifetimes, execution, execution_status, disassembly_table, instruction_events, source_checkpoints, trace_gaps, instruction_count, coverage, storage, heap_history, stage_results, resource_usage, execution_limits, tracing_configuration, optional type_registry, source_metadata, evidence_fusion, crash_report, valgrind_report, and sanitizer_report. Option/null and missing optional/defaulted fields are not evidence of successful capture. schema_version=2 covers supported V2.1/V2.2; the four older pre-V2.1 example documents with removed limit keys are not supported on import. Deprecated per-instruction register observations are parse-only: new output omits them. Identity domains Domain Where recorded What it is not --------- Snapshot vector index / step_index snapshotsi GDB stop counter or instruction attempt GDB stop_id Snapshot observation, event before/after, journal wrapper Snapshot index; not necessarily consecutive instruction_position, instruction_count Stop/gap/trace Retained event position; journal-only can retain zero in JSON event_id / event vector position instruction_eventsj instruction_id (disassembly table) or unique source line checkpoint_id InstructionEvent Exact execution at that stop; only most recent checkpoint tag source_checkpointsn RecordingData Duplicated snapshot; it stores snapshot index allocation_id, old_allocation_id Heap events, state, lifetime Process address, event index or pointer provenance; 0 untracked sequence, pid Heap runtime Stop/event positions; sequences start per PID activation_id, lexical_scope_id Frame/variable Source variable name or address address, points_to, next_address Memory/event/variable Identity; numeric addresses can recur Heap records HeapEvent stores event_type=allocatedreallocatedfreedallocation_failed, per-PID sequence, pid, allocation_id, optional old_allocation_id, address, size, caller and detail. AllocationLifetime stores allocation ID, PID, allocation sequence and optional free sequence. HeapBlockInfo stores final/historical state and optionally realloc_from_id; each snapshot can store alive heap_blocks as observed at a stop. These are complementary, not one-to-one byte replicas. Successful realloc requires relationship verification(parser-validation.htmlrealloc-link-verification). HeapHistoryCoverage.complete is scoped to verified observed event PIDs plus followed inferior, with unknown descendants. Level 3 · Accurate field-level examples The following is a projection of fields from a captured phase8b_defined.c run, not a complete importable trace. OS-specific PID/address values differ between runs. Its first two events describe an in-place realloc that starts a new lifetime ID; the third frees the successor: json {"sequence":1,"allocation_id":1,"old_allocation_id":null,"event_type":"allocated","address":"0x705010","size_bytes":12} {"sequence":2,"allocation_id":2,"old_allocation_id":1,"event_type":"reallocated","address":"0x705010","size_bytes":16} {"sequence":3,"allocation_id":2,"old_allocation_id":null,"event_type":"freed","address":"0x705010","size_bytes":16} raw_bytes_hex="0a000000" at an audited stop is a byte capture, not proof the C initializer ran. A separately recorded PointerTarget can report address_match_allocation_id=1 and allocation_id=null, because address containment is not origin. To load a full trace, run the CLI walkthrough(usage.htmllevel-2-run-a-recording); do not paste these projections into TraceStore::open. NOTE: JSON export's max_json_export_bytes bounds the serialized document; neither that nor the parser's input cap bounds already assembled engine trace RAM. Resource policy(engine-limits.htmllevel-2-budgets-across-stages) lists the separate limits.

title: Stage 2 handoff & limits
summary: Stage 2 handoff · guarantees, limits and glossary Level 1 · Intuition Stage 1 hands future consumers a validated, immutable, bounded-query evidence source, not a complete reconstruction of C program meaning. A sound trace can be p
text: Stage 2 handoff · guarantees, limits and glossary Level 1 · Intuition Stage 1 hands future consumers a validated, immutable, bounded-query evidence source, not a complete reconstruction of C program meaning. A sound trace can be partial; an observed object can have uncertain origin. Stage 2 may derive explanations while displaying their evidence and qualifications, but must never turn a missing observation into a fact. {{diagram:handoff}} Level 2 · The freeze contract - Load a supported schema-v2 document through TraceStore; remember ingestion is schema-only. Call validated_semantic() and inspect report().is_structurally_sound(), is_partial() and individual findings. - Share the canonical Arc<DebugSessionTrace/Arc<TraceIndexes via cloned TraceStore; use borrowed records and same-trace EvidenceRef, not numeric IDs from another execution. - Page checkpoint variables, events and diagnostics using explicit half-open ranges no wider than 128; request all subsequent pages. Distinguish Unavailable, empty evidence and an actual error. - Maintain separate execution status, attempted/retained events, gaps, byte readability, lexical scope, initialization (often unknown), heap-history/observed PID scope and semantic relationship confidence. - Keep heap realloc links dependent on recorded event and same-PID lifetime boundaries; no predecessor from numeric address equality. Never equate pointer containment to origin, AST syntax to execution, Valgrind source site to primary-run allocation ID or scoped PID completion to complete descendants. Level 3 · Concrete API handoff rust let view = store.validated_semantic(); if !view.report().is_structurally_sound() { // Display contradictory imported relationships, not a definite explanation. } let scope = view.process_coverage(); // descendants remain unavailable let stop = view.checkpoint_summary(snapshot_index)?; let _ = (scope.unobserved_descendants, stop.reference.location()); This is a body excerpt using public APIs from src/trace_parser/{semantic,consumer,evidence}.rs; follow the complete runnable example(usage.htmllevel-3-load-and-validate). The API tables(api.htmllevel-3-signatures-and-contracts) list query signatures; validation(parser-validation.htmlrealloc-link-verification) covers adversarial realloc imports. Stage 2 is future work: no new execution interpreter, provenance graph, byte initialization detector, GUI or data model is provided by this site. Performance (not a guarantee) In the independent Stage 1 release-profile audit, a 3.337 MB, 900-snapshot / 3,143-real-instruction-event trace took approximately 48 ms median typed parse, 1.13 ms index build, 0.555 ms once-only semantic validation and ~17 MiB parser-process RSS after indexing across three runs. A 461 KB small trace took ~8.27 ms parse and ~0.264 ms index build. The index estimate for the heavy sample was 28,369 bytes, not process RSS; per-query TP-7 measurements reported zero allocations but once-only validation allocated. Host, allocator and workload variation are material; these are not Stage 2 latency commitments. Input/JSON byte limits do not bound total RAM. See limits(engine-limits.html). Known limitations 1. Coverage: user-code, selected-thread and followed-inferior stop scope; gaps, no complete all-thread or fork-descendant instruction timeline; silent children unknown. 2. Heap: only linked-object allocator wrappers and accepted telemetry; incomplete transport/ACK or legacy metadata lowers confidence. Pointer address containment is not allocation provenance. Historical bytes never get rewritten by later frees/reuse. 3. Static/diagnostic: AST candidates do not prove expression execution. DWARF metadata may be missing. Valgrind and sanitizers are independent processes; equal source/address does not establish primary allocation identity. 4. Memory: readable GDB bytes and lexical scope do not prove C initialization; unattempted or capped tails are not silently decoded. 5. Resources/portability: no sandbox, hard total-engine-RAM guarantee or full parser streaming/seek index. Linux x86-64/GCC/GDB-supported evidence is not a universal cross-platform promise. Four pre-V2.1 files with removed fields remain unsupported on import. Glossary Term Meaning ------ Checkpoint Retained stopped snapshot; not every program instruction or stop Stop ID Processed GDB stop counter, distinct from vector/attempt indices Event position Index into canonical retained event array; never invent missing entries Gap Interval where instruction capture lacks exact events; unknown count Allocation lifetime Trace-local observed identity with PID/sequence boundaries, not an address Provenance Evidence of where a pointer originated; containment alone is insufficient EvidenceRef Weak-trace-identity citation to a canonical record; not portable Definite Verified specific observation/relation under its documented scope Candidate / Ambiguous Plausible unproved relation / multiple compatible relations Unavailable / Contradictory Insufficient evidence / structurally rejected relationship Partial coverage Some observations missing; does not mean record corruption Independent diagnostic Valgrind or sanitizer output from another execution WARNING: The approved Stage 1 freeze authorizes a qualified input for future semantic work, not permission to collapse these terms into a single “trace complete” flag. See the final integrated audit(../stage1-final-audit.md) for verification scope.
